reason: The regular people (Israelites) in this passage are primarily portrayed through their fears, doubts, and complaints rather than through favorable qualities. They are depicted as being greatly afraid (וַיִּֽירְאוּ֙ מְאֹ֔ד), crying out in distress, and expressing regret about leaving Egypt—even suggesting they would have preferred continued enslavement (חֲדַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וְנַֽעַבְדָ֣ה אֶת־ מִצְרָֽיִם). While the narrative concludes with them believing in God and Moses (וַיַּֽאֲמִ֙ינוּ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְמֹשֶׁ֖ה), the preponderance of the passage emphasizes human frailty, faithlessness, and complaint rather than noble or courageous qualities. The favorable portrayal applies more to Moses (as leader) and God's intervention than to the regular people themselves.
